title: Joining Danny White's band at the Club Sands
summary: How he got in as bass player and arranger, and who was in the band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah. And how I started playing with Danny White, see, Danny White had a band, and they had Irvin Bannister, Ernest Hollins, Hulk, Henry Hawkins, the trumpet player. Henry Hawkins, yeah, Hawkins. Yeah, yeah. And Irvin Bannister and Joe Fox in the band, you know. And so he got this job on St. Charles Avenue with the club Sands, you know. And Danny said, man, I need a bass player, you know. And Ernest Hollins told him, so why not get Curtis, man. See, I was the last one in Danny's band. He had all the rest of those guys. And they learned a true year on piano. True year?
Leonard True year, yeah. True year, okay.
Lawrence Cotton was in his band later? Yeah, he came later. Okay.
Just like when he got George Davis later and also Leo Nelson Taylor later.

And then he got Teddy Riley too. Well anyway, he told him to get Missy because man, this guy's the only player say he arranges too, you know. And so when I first got with the band Danny and them men, they looked like they couldn't play ABC, you know. And Ernest Hollins, they hadn't read no music since they left Booker T. Washington High School, you know. And the first arrangement I made for him, it was whole notes, whole notes were real slow notes and they was having trouble with that man, whole and half notes. One time when we were playing there, they had a guy that had a song on the box by Ray Charles. Let me see the name of this song.
